title: Inter Alia
wpTitle: Inter Alia Review Round-up – Starring Rosamund Pike at the National Theatre

ratings.excerpt: Pike is on peak form in a tsunami of middle class angst … Plot-wise, you can see what’s coming down the tracks. But the tension builds nicely and is brilliantly executed. … Pike is electric in this, a neveroff-stage performance that communicates courage, comedy, principled conviction and a tsunami of middle-class angst. The evening is an absolute banger. It sent a chill down my spine, and it’ll be a smash hit for the National Theatre.

Rosamund Pike rules in searing legal drama from Prima Facie team … With anarchic energy, Pike plays a judge whose world is upended in a companion drama to Suzie Miller’s hit, again directed by Justin Martin … This is an almost deliberate counterpoint to Prima Facie... Miller wanted to highlight how poorly the law serves victims, and Inter Alia presents the same issue from the flipside with a female judge, determined to make the system more just, whose world is upended by an accusation close to home. … All the hallmarks of Justin Martin’s pulsating direction are here, from the onstage guitar and drums ratcheting up the tension to Pike’s physical, occasionally anarchic performance. … Jessica remains the moral and emotional centre: her tragedy unfolds like that of an Ibsen protagonist failed

Rosamund Pike is riveting in Inter Alia at the National Theatre … The actor commands the stage for over two hours in Suzie Miller’s play about toxic masculinity inside and outside the courtroom … Rosamund Pike gives a hectic, vital, riveting performance at the centre of Suzie Miller’s gut-punch of a play, as a judge, Jess Parks, who discovers that the toxic masculinity she sees in the courtroom has taken root in her own home. … Inter Alia shares DNA as well as a title drawn from Latin legalese with Miller’s previous play, Prima Facie... Both plays are a little schematic and necessarily enmeshed in the nuances of the legal world (Miller was a lawyer before she was a writer). Both pack a powerful, sobering punch. The screen star gives a gale force performance as a troubled high court judge in this companion piece to Jodie Comer smash ‘Prima Facie’ … It’s a breathless performance from Pike, who crests and surges from neuroticism to icy confidence. Rosamund Pike is immaculate in her return to the stage after 15 years … Inter Alia at the National is theatre’s gut-wrenching spin on Adolescence … Inter Alia has a lot in common with its agenda-setting predecessor... It grips, too, and is gut-wrenching, but in comparison feels sketchier. … Once again, the piece calls for a transfixing, shape-shifting performance from its star, and the hurtling 105-minute action showcases Pike’s theatrical bravura. She can hold a stage as vast as the National Theatre’s Lyttelton with immaculate assurance. … Glover and Talbot bring a brusque reticence and contrasting despair to their roles but the script positions them almost as peripheral.

Rosamund Pike is immaculate as a judge staring down her own hypocrisy in Inter Alia … The duo behind West End hit ‘Prima Facie’ reunite for another searing play about sexual assault and legal injustice … After playing a delightfully brittle matriarch in Saltburn (2023), Rosamund Pike paints an infinitely more complex portrait of motherhood in this brilliantly tense, emotive drama. … ... this time the tone is less crusading, more complexifying, as a female judge is forced to stare down her own hypocrisy. … Like Netflix’s smash hit Adolescence, Inter Alia is calculated to strike fear into the hearts of parents (of boys, especially). Still, it’s softer, too, offering a sympathetic portrait of a teenager sent astray by pressuring school friends and low self-worth. … Sometimes, it teeters dange

Rosamund Pike is a force of nature in Inter Alia … Suzie Miller's new play about a Crown Court judge whose son is accused of rape is vital and damningly topical … It is a stomach-churning watch, with Jasper Talbot as Harry physically unravelling in the play’s final scenes. Under Martin’s direction, the 100-minute, no-interval running time hurtles forward with gripping, taut intensity. … And at the centre is Pike: a force of nature. She never stops moving, keeping up with household chores as she talks, ferociously dashing from work to home and back again. Her heart breaks as everything she thought she knew about her child slips through her fingers. By the final blackout, the verdict is clear: this is a damningly topical and vital drama that needs to be heard.

All rise for Rosamund: Pike's a force of nature in electrifying sequel to hit courtroom drama … Rosamund Pike was sensational on Wednesday night as a High Court judge in a new play at the National Theatre by Australian writer Suzie Miller … The only thing that rankled with me is the play's presumption that we are enchanted by Jessica's middle-class values and 'parenting style'. Even so, Inter Alia – whose title means 'among other things' – plays out like a Greek tragedy. … Increasingly uncomfortable to watch, just like Prima Facie it will keep the chattering classes chattering long into the night.

Rosamund Pike holds court in National Theatre debut … ... Inter Alia puts new subjects on the stand, too: working motherhood, adolescent sex, and the dark spectre of social media. The result is a play with the power to both galvanise and paralyse with fear – especially for those raising kids. … Masterfully directed by Justin Martin (who also helmed Prima Facie), Pike also relishes a script which beautifully captures the singularity of motherhood … Miriam Buether’s set masterfully reflects the darkness and danger lurking behind perceived domestic normality. … ... Miller gives us provocation without polemics

Rosamund Pike shines but this play feels like a lecture … Suzie Miller’s follow-up to the smash hit Prima Facie features a remarkable central performance and a headline-grabbing theme but it’s rather slender fare … Sometimes there’s a fine line between a play and a pamphlet. Elements of both fight it out in the punchy new offering … Pike will surely be in line for the big prizes at the end of the year. In an interval-free piece that is more monologue than straight play, she’s forever centre stage … Justin Martin — who also directed Prima Facie — ensures that the tempo never falters. It’s an intensely choreographed evening … Inter Alia, like Adolescence, will no doubt get conversations rolling, which is no bad thing. Blunt-edged and formulaic … Rosamund Pike sparkles as a beleaguered judge in a clod-hopping feminism-lite drama … Now it falls to Rosamund Pike to offer similar heft to Miller and Martin’s similarly themed latest collaboration – and unfortunately, although she tackles the central role with celerity, sincerity and considerable wit, the task proves beyond her. The blame is not Pike’s. … .... the bulk of the piece is written in direct-address narration, with the two men little more than walk-ons; it’s almost as if Miller doesn’t trust herself to write actual dialogue.
